doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: What is hip? Cannonball and the Hipster lyric
summary: Monk asks about hipness; Sidran recites his lyric Don't Cry for No Hipster.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: This has been a most fascinating conversation. And of course I didn’t get to everything but I want to end with — well maybe this is a philosophical question. My musical hero is Cannonball Adderley and he said on record, “Hipness is not a state of mind, it’s a fact of life.”
And Tower of Power said, “Hipness is what it is, sometimes it’s what it ain’t.” So Mr. Sidran, can you tell me what is hip?

Tell me, tell me. I love what Cannonball said. I really, I remember the record. And I remember hearing it the first time and saying this man is a teacher boy. What is hip. Yeah you know so don’t cry for no hipster, he knew what he signed up for. The look in the field, the rundown appeal, the passing ship the distant shore. Don’t cry for no hipster, he saw the writing on the wall and it gave him hope, just another slippery slope, a deeper truth he can’t recall. And when young becomes old and cool turns to cold, that’s when © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

we’ll see if the truth can set him free. Until then don’t cry for no hipster. He had his day and he had his night. And, I’ve got to conflate the ending — let’s call it what it is, in a world like his it’s usually the wrongs that make it right. That’s as close as I could come.
